dedupe_keys.name: us test system with high spatial and temporal resolution for renewable integration studies

description: This open test system represents the power system of the contiguous United States at high spatial and temporal resolution for renewable integration and transition planning studies. It was built by Yixing Xu, Nathan Myhrvold, Daniel J. Olsen and co-authors using only publicly available data, and it was validated by running it in a production cost model and comparing results with historical generation. It provides the grid with cost curves and transmission capacities, and time series of demand and renewable output that represent variability, and the method to build such systems is described in a paper presented at the 2020 IEEE PES General Meeting. Coverage is the United States at bus level with hourly profiles. The data are one ZIP of about 969 MB with Tabular Data Package metadata on Zenodo (version 0.4.2, February 2021) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost, with a version history of cost curve and transmission changes. Caveats: the grid is built from public data and approximates real infrastructure, and it has not been updated since 2021. Simulation uses are production cost modelling, transmission and storage expansion and decarbonisation studies. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
